claims.label: Title of the work
Homage to Lokeśvara
Tārā, liberator of all saṃsāra, receives homage
Statement of authorial purpose
Aspiration that obstacles be pacified
Classification: unsurpassed yoga tantra
Further classification: a yoginī tantra
Family classification: the Vajra-Supreme-Horse family
Identified as Bhagavatī Tārā's tantra, sovereign of the family-wheel
This praise held to be the complete tantra itself

Opening gloss identifying the first verse
"Homage" as the basis for the whole discourse

Etymology of "Mother" and "Heroine"

Tārā's origin from Avalokiteśvara's lotus-face pollen

Opening gloss identifying the fourth verse

Vāyu as the one who shapes the world's particulars

The vidyā-mantra spoken by Ārya Tārā

Opening gloss identifying the eighth verse

Crescent-moon crown ornament

Opening gloss identifying the thirteenth verse

Opening gloss identifying the fourteenth verse
Strikes the great earth and Mount Meru with her clapping palm

Wrathful frown and a terrifying HŪM proclaimed through her nostrils

Opening gloss identifying the fifteenth verse

She establishes beings in the domain of non-abiding nirvāṇa
